posts.name: The Girl With No Name
posts.cooked:
Most of the cutoff issue I have is because I'm in another timezone, honestly. For instance, while the show drops on Tuesday for most, that's 2 or 3am on Wednesday for me. When C&A do give a cutoff (which seems to be a little rarer nowadays), I inevitably get confused about the actual date I can submit it, and end up missing the deadline. It's not something anyone intelligent can miss, but I'm not anyone intelligent, ha ha. 

 

Honestly, if they just made cutoff times more obvious to check, it would solve 90% of my issue with this change. As is, without being able to do Patreon things (not for monetary reasons, but security ones... I'd rather not say), I'm stuck wondering not just if my letter will be picked, but if I actually get the opportunity to hear the answer.

posts.name: Cult of Gloom
posts.cooked:
The main legitimate problem I am seeing people having is that they might ask a question and have it answered in an editor's notes they won't see, but I personally thought it was a pretty safe assumption that editors notes will become a patreon only question kind of thing.

 

I also really don't think a dollar for the extra episode at the end of each month is asking that much, and I really don't think it was born out of greed. You don't get into this buisness for greed, its a terrible way to make large sums of money. If there are non-monetary concerns around using patreon though I can see how that would be frustrating.

Cult of Gloom:

The main legitimate problem I am seeing people having is that they might ask a question and have it answered in an editor's notes they won't see, but I personally thought it was a pretty safe assumption that editors notes will become a patreon only question kind of thing. I also really don't think a dollar for the extra episode at the end of each month is asking that much, and I really don't think it was born out of greed.

I do feel like "assume good faith" is something people could kinda stand to adopt as a stance as of late. There's a few too many cases as of late where what I sometimes agree are reasonable concerns are buried under the hostility of assuming the issues in question came about as a result of the GTG folks deliberately trying to cause harm, when I've never seen the GTG folks do anything to make that feel like a justified stance.

I do think the GTG folks are sometimes guilty of Didn't Think This Through (which is likely what happened here), but that's still not deserving of the accusations of deliberate  malfeasance  thrown out there versus just civilly pointing out the issue and some suggestions on how to deal with it.

posts.name: cnranger
posts.cooked:
Matchstickman:

My perception is not that it's adding content for the patreon backers, it's taking away already established content from non-patreons. 

As usual I'm feeling multiple side of the issue.

  • I think the quote from Matchstickman explains why it leaves a bad taste in my mouth. If Editor's Notes were new and behind the paywall, no problem. If they had always costed, no problem. But since they were free and now they are not, it feels wrong. It also sounds really entitled to say "because I got this for free before I deserve to get it free forever."

  • There are really two ways to fund a podcast these days, listener support or ads. I feel the listener support is by far the better way.

  • Its only 12 bucks, that's skipping eating out 1 time a year basically, for me. However I don't like things withdrawing automatically from my account, why can't I pay 12 dollars now and be good for the year? That would sit much better with me. Is that an option Patreon veteran?

  • Personally I've decided to not particiate in the Patreon, deciding the "cost" was not worth the "goods" provided. I will sorely miss the Editor's Notes but I realize that is a consequence of my own personal choice (one that I can choose to change). I will continue enjoying the free content for as long as it exists and continue buying many things Sentinels.

  • Finally the setting up of the Patreon and the reflection of it was worth it to me to donate has led me to the conclusion that I would prefer the Letter's Page to come to end than pay monthly for it. Sad and as I noted above perhaps entitled.
